claims.claim: Every connected cograph other than a singleton or a graph with exactly one universal vertex is equivalent to the zero game.
claims.evidence: In the canonical top join decomposition of a nontrivial connected cograph, singleton join blocks are exactly universal vertices. With at least two universal vertices, pairing any two dominates every vertex. With no universal vertex, every join block has at least two vertices; choosing a,b in one block and c,d in another makes (a,b),(c,d) a pairing dominating set, because the first block lies in N[c]∩N[d] and every other block lies in N[a]∩N[b]. Source Remark 9 therefore makes the component equivalent to zero.
claims.witness: Exact minimax enumeration confirmed score (0,0), including within disconnected contexts, for all 1,199 relevant connected labeled cographs on at most six vertices.
claims.search_method: Direct cotree case analysis plus exhaustive integer minimax enumeration of every labeled cograph through six vertices; no web search.

claims.claim: SHVG on cographs is polynomially equivalent to an explicit open-or-delete scoring game on rooted forests.
claims.evidence: For a unique universal vertex u, a strategy-transposition argument works in every disjoint context: replacing a proposed move x by u either preserves the final coloring when the simulated player later obtains u, or improves the relevant player's objective because a Breaker-owned universal vertex forces the entire component's contribution to zero. Thus u dominates other moves for both players. Breaker taking u leaves a zero position. After Maker takes u, C-u has at least two vertices and contains twins a,b. Applying source Theorem 13 in both C with u Maker-owned and C-u assigns a to Maker and b to Breaker; b spoils u, while every vertex of C-u has exactly the same happiness condition in both positions. Hence Maker's move exposes precisely C-u. Conversely, adjoining a new universal vertex to the disjoint child realizations and a zero K2 ballast realizes each internal project; the ballast ensures uniqueness of the new universal vertex whenever the internal node has children, and zero projects can be omitted. The construction uses L+3I vertices and polynomially many edges.
claims.witness: For all 6,039 labeled cographs on at most six vertices, including disconnected sums, exact graph minimax scores agreed with the recursively constructed forest scores for both starters.
claims.search_method: Direct contextual strategy audit using the source minimax definition, Remark 9, and Theorem 13, supplemented by exhaustive graph-versus-forest comparison; no web search.

claims.claim: Both starting-player variants on arbitrary reduced forests are threshold-preservingly reducible with linear node blowup to Maker-first play on a single rooted tree; consequently SHVG on all cographs is polynomially equivalent to Maker-first SHVG on connected cographs.
claims.evidence: For Z=S1, both starting scores are zero, so Z is equivalent to zero and M(R(F+Z))=B(F). For the Maker-first reduction, let F contain L prize leaves and D=S_(2L+2). Deleting D from the Breaker position F+D leaves M(F)≤L. If Breaker deletes any root T of F instead, Maker can open D, leaving Breaker on (F-T)+(2L+2)A. The source sum bound gives value at least B(F-T)+B((2L+2)A)≥L+1. Thus D is uniquely optimal for Breaker, B(F+D)=M(F), and M(R(F+D))=M(F). Since L≤|F|, both trees have linear size. Their cograph realizations are connected, while the reverse reduction is inclusion.
claims.witness: The checker tested both identities on 210 small forests, including the empty forest and forests containing nested projects, with exact threshold-preserving score equality.
claims.search_method: Symbolic minimax and size-bound verification, followed by exhaustive exact testing of representative forests; no web search.

claims.claim: The cograph game is linear-time solvable when every tree in the reduced forest has outdegree at most two.
claims.evidence: Inductively, each child project is equivalent to zero or A. An internal node with zero or one A-child has both starting scores zero and is therefore zero. With two A-children, opening exposes 2A, which has equal scores one and is the constant-one game; deletion gives zero, so the project has the same options and value as A in every context. The top forest consequently reduces to z copies of A, with scores ceil(z/2) and floor(z/2). One bottom-up Boolean label per reduced node gives linear running time after the standard linear cotree construction.
claims.witness: Exact recurrence checks covered 191 binary rooted trees through nine nodes and 1,820 small forests of such trees; every score matched the claimed A/zero labeling.
claims.search_method: Structural induction on rooted projects plus exhaustive exact minimax checks of trees and contextual sums; no web search.

claims.claim: Reduced forests of height one—equivalently, disjoint unions of stars and isolated vertices after zero components are removed—admit an O(n^2) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: For j≤k, the stated exchange comparison follows by simultaneous induction for both starters: exposed-leaf moves and moves in other stars are mirrored and invoke the smaller-state hypothesis, while opening the distinguished stars reaches the same state with l+j+k exposed leaves. The accompanying monotonicity in star size makes deletion of the largest star optimal for Breaker. Hence Maker need consider only taking an exposed leaf or opening the largest star, and Breaker only deleting an exposed leaf or the largest star, yielding exactly the two displayed recurrences. Remaining prize count never exceeds the initial K, so there are O(rK)=O(n^2) states and constant work per state after sorting.
claims.witness: The claimed recurrence matched unrestricted exact minimax on 8,712 height-one states: up to five stars with every size from 2 through 8 and up to ten exposed leaves.
claims.search_method: Exchange-induction audit, state-count analysis, and exhaustive comparison against the unrestricted forest recurrence; no web search.

claims.claim: The pair of standalone scores (Ms,Bs) is insufficient as a cotree dynamic-programming state.
claims.evidence: P3=S2 and K1,3=S3 both have standalone scores (1,0). Nevertheless, exact minimax gives P3+P3=(1,1) and P3+K1,3=(2,1). Replacing a component using only its identical standalone pair would have to treat these two sums identically, so that pair cannot be compositional.
claims.witness: The checker reproduces P3+P3=(1,1) and P3+K1,3=(2,1) from the unrestricted recurrence.
claims.search_method: Direct finite game-tree evaluation of the two components and their contextual sums; no web search.

claims.claim: For every integer r≥1, two height-two rooted projects have the same 4r+2 nodes, 4r prize leaves, height, outdegree multiset, and standalone scores (r,0), yet adjoining one prize leaf gives scores (r,1) and (r+1,1), respectively.
claims.evidence: For k≥2, Breaker can obtain B(lA+S_k)≤ceil(l/2) by deleting S_k. If Breaker deletes a leaf, Maker opens S_k and obtains at least floor((l-1+k)/2)≥ceil(l/2), proving equality. Applying this identity to X_r=R((2r-1)A+S_(2r+1)) and Y_r=R(2rA+S_(2r)) gives standalone scores (r,0). Both have 4r leaves plus two internal nodes, height two, and internal outdegrees 2r and 2r+1. The two possible first moves after adjoining A give contextual values (r,1) and (r+1,1), including the r=1 boundary.
claims.witness: Integer minimax verified every asserted invariant and score for r=1 through 12; at r=1 the contextual pairs are (1,1) and (2,1).
claims.search_method: Algebraic proof for arbitrary integer r plus deterministic exact checks over twelve parameter values; no web search.

claims.claim: Breaker's strict preference between two rooted-project types can reverse with the surrounding forest, so no rule whose choice between those roots depends only on their individual types can always prescribe an optimal deletion.
claims.evidence: For U=S4 and V=R(2A+U), exact recurrence gives M(U)=2, M(V)=1, M(2U)=2, and M(U+V)=3. Thus in U+V, deleting U leaves value 1 while deleting V leaves 2, making U uniquely optimal. In 2U+V, deleting U leaves M(U+V)=3 while deleting V leaves M(2U)=2, making V uniquely optimal. The same pair of project types therefore has opposite strict order in the two contexts.
claims.witness: The checker also reproduces the auxiliary values B(4A+V)=2 and B(2A+2U)=3 and all four post-deletion values 1,2,3,2.
claims.search_method: Complete exact evaluation of every legal root choice in the two displayed forests; no web search.

target_evidence: The source target requires either a polynomial-time algorithm for all cographs or a matching hardness theorem. The draft proves an exact rooted-forest equivalence, reductions to connected Maker-first instances, two genuine tractable subclasses, and compositional counterexamples, but it explicitly leaves arbitrary rooted trees unresolved and expressly disclaims a complete classification. These are material correct advances, not a resolution of the entire target; its claimed PARTIAL status is accurate.
